messages:
incident-bot: Paging alert: SLO breach detected for inference/continuous-batching in us-west-2. metric=p99_latency window=5m value=3.8s SLO=2.0s. Severity: P1. Runbook: <https://redwood-internal/runbooks/cont-batch-p99>

alice (oncall): oncall here, ack. seeing the alert pop ~10:12UTC. adding logs + triage now.

grace (observability): Grafana link: <https://grafana/internal/d/contbatch/p99> - heatmap shows a tail starting ~10:06UTC, correlates with a burst of long-seq requests (seq_len > 2048) hitting contbatch path. p95 is ~420ms but p99 shoots up.

bob (eng-runtime): I can repro locally on a canary. Scheduler queue depth spikes when a few >2k token requests enter. Continuous batching is aggregating them and blocking streaming workers. Looks like fairness scoring weights small sequences higher so large ones are getting stuck and then block prefetch/KV cache hot path.

claire (eng-sre): customer-impact check: no 5xxs, but several streaming sessions reported stalls. Running incident impact scan now for customers with >500ms error budgets consumed in last 15m.

frank (support): two customers filed tickets: acme-ai and studybot. They report “streaming endpoint hangs for ~6s intermittently.” marking them as affected.

dan (ml-infra): quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce CONTBATCH_MAX_BATCH to 32 from 128 for us-west-2 pools; 2) enable per-request preemption (contbatch_preempt=true) to allow streaming to break big batches; 3) route seq_len>1024 to slowlane pool (dedicated nodes) until we tune scheduler.

alice (oncall): implemented step 1 (temporarily set CONTBATCH_MAX_BATCH=32) on pool contbatch-usw2-alpha via remote-config. patch propagated at 10:18UTC. Observability: queue depth immediately dropped.

grace (observability): after change p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 1.9s in next 2 minutes. still above SLO target but much improved. p95 unchanged.

bob (eng-runtime): preparing a hotfix to adjust fairness weights. Small sequences were getting preferred scheduling; will change fairness exponent and add explicit sequence-length bucketing to avoid head-of-line blocking. Draft PR: <https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/8942>

claire (eng-sre): running canary of preemption flag now. dan, can you flip contbatch_preempt=true in canary for 5min and monitor streaming stalls? If stable, we'll rollout.

dan (ml-infra): flipping in canary now... done at 10:23UTC. Preemption reduced streaming stalls in canary to near zero.

alice (oncall): rolling contbatch_preempt=true to all us-west-2 pools. patch applied 10:26UTC.

grace (observability): p99 back to 1.1s after preemption rollout. trending toward SLO. adding dashboards to track per-customer long-seq ratio.

frank (support): pinging affected customers: acme-ai contact says perf improved, still sees occasional 1.5s stalls (was 6s). marked tickets with mitigation notes.

erin (product): please keep me posted on customer impact and whether we need crediting / SLA notes. If any large customers still affected escalate to account team.

bob (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: a sequence-length imbalance (thundering large sequences) plus fairness metric that didn't preempt long-running batches caused head-of-line blocking. Fixes: short-term config knobs (batch size, preempt), mid-term fair-scheduler + seq bucketing, long-term KV cache improvements to reduce block durations.

alice (oncall): creating followup tasks: TICKET-1428 adjust fairness scheduler + seq bucketing; TICKET-1429 add per-customer throttles for long-seq to avoid noisy neighbors; TICKET-1430 add automated routing rule for seq_len>1024 to slowlane. Assigning to bob/dan.

bob (eng-runtime): coding plan: change fairness exponent -> 0.6, add seq-buckets [0-256,257-1024,1025-4096,>4096], and set strict max-batch-per-bucket. will run perf test in staging.

claire (eng-sre): postmortem note: this was a service-level degradation, no data loss. Severity downgraded to P2 after mitigations; will keep incident active until followups in progress.

alice (oncall): handing over to night oncall @dan in 30m. leaving sticky notes: 1) contbatch knobs we flipped (CONTBATCH_MAX_BATCH=32, contbatch_preempt=true), 2) PR link, 3) TICKET-* numbers above. If anything regresses revert preempt flag and scale up dedicated slowlane pool.

dan (ml-infra): ack handoff. I'll watch overnight and pick up the followups tomorrow. If p99 creeps >2.0s, escalate to eng-runtime immediately. Setting a page rule to re-alert if p99 >2.0s for 3 consecutive 1m windows.

deploy-bot: Automated note: rolled config to contbatch-usw2-alpha at 10:18UTC, contbatch_preempt rollout at 10:26UTC. No failed nodes detected.

grace (observability): saved event timeline + snapshot to incident channel. Link: <https://grafana/internal/snapshots/contbatch-1837654321>

frank (support): updated tickets with resolution steps and contact info, leaving them open for 24hrs to confirm customer recovery.

erin (product): thanks all. pls include customer communication draft in postmortem. Noting potential commercial impact for any long-standing SLO misses.

alice (oncall): closing immediate mitigation. we'll keep incident open for the change tasks until tickets are done. handing thread to @dan. :wave:

claire (eng-sre): adding final note: when we implement seq bucketing, add telemetry to track per-bucket latency percentiles to ensure we don't regress small-seq latency while protecting streaming.

dan (ml-infra): confirmed receipt. night watch starting 10:45UTC. will ping if any anomalies.
